analysis.title: Federal Reserve preview: A pause before a December hike
key_insights: ING expects the Fed to hold rates at the 28 October FOMC meeting, in line with markets and economists, despite hot September inflation prints.

The September core CPI print of 0.3% month-on-month briefly pushed October hike odds above 50%. Comments from Vice Chairs Jefferson and Bowman and Governor Waller signalling no rush, plus Chair Warsh not talking up action at the IMF meetings in Bangkok, calmed markets.

The latest SEP showed four FOMC members projecting 50bp of hikes between now and year-end, so the October decision is unlikely to be unanimous. Hammack, Kashkari and Logan voted to hike in July and could dissent again in favour of hiking.

ING expects a brief press release and a short, matter-of-fact Warsh press conference. The message would be that the economy is in decent shape, unemployment is low, inflation is above target, and policy depends on incoming data with probably more work to do.

ING forecasts a 25bp hike in December, leaving the Fed funds range at 4-4.25%, followed by a pause through December 2027 when the December 2026 hike is reversed. This matches consensus. The Fed's own projections show one hike this year and no change in 2027.

November CPI is released the day after the Fed meeting and officials will likely see it first, so they will have more information than the market. Two jobs reports and one inflation print come before the December decision.

ING's path assumes that in the months after the midterm elections an agreement improves energy flow from the Persian Gulf and sharply cuts shipping and insurance costs. That would lower pump prices while refineries run at capacity. With wage growth near 3% and housing (35% of the inflation basket) disinflating, ING sees inflation back at 2% in 2H 2027.

Risks are tilted toward a longer-lasting conflict. ING would not rule out additional hikes in 1Q 2027. In that scenario squeezed households and higher yields raise the risk of a weaker economy, and eventual cuts in 2H 2027 would be swifter and larger than in the base case.

Treasuries rallied over the past week, with the 10-year yield falling below 5% after an earlier break above 5.25%. ING doubts the move persists and expects the yield to return above 5% on inflation, fiscal deficit and AI-boom pressures, though timing is uncertain. The risk-off tone and the sell-off in French bonds make a hold more likely.

A plan to shrink the Fed balance sheet, a policy objective for Warsh, is likely still some way off. Committee recommendations are expected closer to the turn of the year. Repo markets are behaving far better than a year ago.

The dollar rose about 4% through September and early October and is now consolidating. Rate differentials are the main driver and have moved slightly against the dollar this month as the US tech sell-off pared back Fed tightening expectations.

Warsh-led FOMC meetings have set the four-to-six-week dollar trend this year: June hawkish, July seen as dovish, September a hawkish hike. ING expects Warsh to stress policy credibility and not conclude that wider credit spreads and softer equities mean fewer hikes are needed, so short-dated US yields stay supported.

ING expects the dollar to hold most of its September gains. A renewed tech-led risk-off move is a more likely catalyst for a dollar decline than dovish Fed messaging. Energy costs and French political risk could pull EUR/USD back to the year's lows near 1.11.

sector_views.rationale: Interest rate-sensitive sectors such as housing are experiencing increasing pain, and mortgage rates may reach new cycle highs if yields rise further.

risk_factors: A longer-lasting Persian Gulf conflict would keep energy prices and inflation high and could bring additional hikes in 1Q 2027.
Higher yields and a squeeze on household spending power would raise the risk of a weaker economy, with new cycle highs for mortgage and corporate borrowing costs.
The November CPI release the day after the FOMC meeting, which officials will likely see first, could surprise markets.
French bond market stress could add systemic pressure.
A renewed tech-led risk-off move could weaken the dollar.
vol_and_positioning: The US tech sell-off and risk-off tone have pared back Fed tightening expectations and pulled the 10-year yield below 5%.
ING notes wider credit spreads and softer equity prices, and expects Warsh not to treat them as grounds for fewer hikes.
geopolitical: Conflict involving the Persian Gulf is raising energy prices. ING's base case assumes a post-midterm agreement that improves Gulf energy flow and cuts shipping and insurance costs, with risks tilted to a longer-lasting conflict.
French bond market weakness and French political risk add to bond angst and pressure on EUR/USD.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish case: inflation is above target, the economy is growing robustly, officials say more tightening is needed, and four FOMC members project 50bp of hikes by year-end.
tension_points.bear_case: Dovish case: recent jobs numbers are disappointing, rate-sensitive sectors like housing are under pain, and the risk-off tone with French bond stress makes tightening unattractive now.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A longer-lasting Persian Gulf conflict would add hikes in 1Q 2027. An energy deal after the midterms that cuts shipping and insurance costs would bring inflation back toward 2% and allow cuts.
